patients.summary: Retired construction foreman on home oxygen for COPD, with alcohol-related cirrhosis, hypertension and diabetes, who joins in 2020. Over six years he is diagnosed with IPF, a Zenker diverticulum, a basal cell carcinoma, an ablated HCC and an unresectable pancreatic adenocarcinoma treated with radiation, and survives three ICU-level admissions and a tension pneumothorax.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
68M here to establish. Previous PCP retired; wife found us through a neighbor. Came in on his portable tank, 2 L.

Lungs: told he has COPD several years back, on continuous O2 2 L by concentrator at home since about 2017, portable for outings. Uses tiotropium every morning and salmeterol twice a day, nebulized albuterol a couple of times a week, more in winter. Gets winded with a flight of stairs, gets the mail fine. No recent steroid bursts that he recalls.

Liver: alcohol-related cirrhosis found on an ultrasound in 2018. Has not had a drink since January 2019. Sees an outside hepatology group twice a year for ultrasound and AFP. Says he was told there were no varices on a scope. Never had fluid or confusion.

BP and sugar: on lisinopril 20, HCTZ 25 and metformin 1000 bid for years. Does not check sugars at home.

C. diff 2019 - hospitalized about a week at an outside hospital, "the worst I've ever felt." No recurrence.

Smoking about 45 pack-years, quit 2014, went back to it for a few months in 2019 and stopped again. Alcohol as above, 4-6 drinks a day for decades before quitting. Retired construction foreman. Married, wife Ingrid.
FHx: father COPD and lung cancer. Mother T2DM. Brother cirrhosis.
PSH: none. NKDA.

Exam: thin, pleasant, mildly dyspneic after walking from the lot, speaking full sentences. BP and SpO2 as charted, on 2 L. No scleral icterus. Distant breath sounds, no wheeze. RRR, no murmur. Abdomen soft, nontender, no ascites appreciated. No asterixis. No edema.

A/P
1. COPD with chronic hypoxemic resp failure on 2 L - continue current inhalers and O2. Will take over DME orders once records are in.
2. Alcoholic cirrhosis, compensated, abstinent - continue hepatology surveillance. Check hep B status for vaccination; will need hep A/B.
3. HTN - at goal. Continue lisinopril/HCTZ.
4. T2DM - A1c today.
5. Hx severe C. diff - noted. Avoid unnecessary antibiotics.
6. Screening: HCV, HIV today. Asking for prior colonoscopy report.

Labs today. Records request sent. RTC 3 months.

events.reason: Records from prior primary care practice

documents.title: Prior Practice Records Summary
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Records from his prior internist, 41 pages, reviewed.

- 2018 abdominal ultrasound: nodular liver contour consistent with cirrhosis, no focal mass, no ascites. Cirrhosis attributed to alcohol.
- 2019 upper endoscopy (outside GI): no esophageal or gastric varices.
- 2019 discharge summary, outside hospital: severe C. difficile colitis, treated, discharged after 7 days.
- 2018 colonoscopy: complete exam, no polyps.
- Home oxygen started 2017 by his prior pulmonary provider, 2 L continuous.
- Med list matches what he told me. Allergies: none.

Nothing else actionable. Colon screening done; with his other issues I do not plan to repeat it.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Mr. Lindqvist, your labs are back. Sugar control is good (A1c in a fine range). Kidney function is normal. Your liver numbers and platelet count look the way they usually do with cirrhosis and are stable compared to the old records. Hepatitis C and HIV tests are negative. You are not immune to hepatitis B, so I would like to start the combined hepatitis A and B vaccine at your next visit. Talk soon.

documents.title: DME oxygen recertification
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Oxygen supplier called, needs new prescriber on file for his concentrator and portable tanks. Order and certificate of medical necessity filled out for PCP signature, 2 L/min continuous, rest and exertion. Faxed back after signature. Pt aware.

documents.title: Primary Care Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
F/u BP/DM. Doing about the same. Breathing at his usual, uses the nebulizer maybe twice a week. Staying home a lot with the pandemic, wife does the shopping. Still no alcohol.
Meds reviewed, no changes. Taking metformin with breakfast and dinner, no GI upset.

BP and sat as charted on 2 L. Lungs distant, no wheeze. Heart regular. No edema. Feet: skin intact, monofilament normal both feet, DP pulses 2+.

A/P: HTN at goal. DM - A1c today. COPD stable on current regimen. Cirrhosis - hepatology ultrasound due next month.
Vaccines: high-dose flu, PCV20 and first Twinrix today. Twinrix #2 in one month at a nurse visit, #3 at 6 months.
RTC 3 months, video is fine.

reports.text: Liver: coarsened echotexture with a nodular contour. No focal hepatic mass. Portal vein patent with hepatopetal flow. Gallbladder without stones. Common bile duct 4 mm. No ascites.
reports.conclusion: Cirrhotic liver morphology. No focal liver lesion.

documents.title: Hepatology Follow-up Letter
documents.author: hepatology
documents.body:
Outside hepatology follow-up, visit date 10/20/2020.

Thank you for allowing us to continue seeing Mr. Lindqvist for alcohol-associated cirrhosis. He remains abstinent since January 2019. No ascites, bleeding or confusion.

Surveillance ultrasound today shows a cirrhotic liver without focal lesion. AFP 3.9. Child-Pugh class A.

Recommendations: continue abstinence; surveillance ultrasound and AFP every 6 months; hepatitis A/B vaccination, which we understand you have started. Variceal screening was negative in 2019; we will repeat endoscopy in the future as indicated.

Allergies: NKDA.

Hepatology

orders.reason: progressive exertional dyspnea, dry cough, clubbing and crackles

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Primary Care Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Dry cough for roughly 3 months, nonproductive, no fever. Breathing is worse with exertion than it was in the fall - now stops halfway up his porch steps, used to do them in one go. No chest pain. No sputum change, no wheeze episodes, nebulizer does not help the cough much. Still on 2 L. No sick contacts.

O: Afebrile. Sat as charted on 2 L, dips with the walk down the hall. Fingers - clubbing, which I do not see documented in his old records. Fine inspiratory crackles at both bases, no wheeze. Heart regular. No edema.

A/P: Progressive exertional dyspnea and dry cough with new clubbing and basal crackles in a former heavy smoker with COPD. This is not his usual COPD picture; concern for an interstitial process. Referring to pulmonology for evaluation (HRCT and full PFTs per them). Continue current inhalers and O2. Labs routine today.
RTC after pulm.

documents.title: Medicare Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Initial AWV.
Functional: independent with self-care, drives short distances, wife manages finances jointly. Uses portable O2 out of the house. No falls in the past year. Hearing fine in conversation. Vision: sees optometry, due for a diabetic eye exam - reminded.
Cognition: clock draw and 3-word recall normal.
Mood: PHQ-2 negative. AUDIT-C 0.
Home safety: no smoking in the home, oxygen safety reviewed, smoke detectors in place.
Advance directives: none on file; he and Ingrid will think about a health care proxy form, given to him.
Prevention: colon screening done 2018, not repeating. PCV20 given 2020. Hep A/B complete. COVID primary series complete. Shingrix and Tdap to do - plan Shingrix in the fall with flu.
Pulmonology appointment is in August.
Care plan given.

events.reason: Progressive dyspnea on exertion and nonproductive cough

reports.text: High-resolution technique with prone and expiratory images. Reticular opacities with honeycombing, predominantly at the lung bases and in the subpleural regions bilaterally. No pulmonary embolism. No consolidation, effusion or other acute process. Heart size normal. No mediastinal adenopathy. No suspicious pulmonary nodule.
reports.conclusion: Basal and subpleural-predominant reticulation with honeycombing, a usual interstitial pneumonia pattern. No acute process.

reports.text: Full pulmonary function testing with lung volumes and diffusion. FEV1 preserved. FVC preserved. FEV1/FVC ratio increased. Total lung capacity, functional residual capacity and residual volume decreased. DLCO reduced. No significant bronchodilator response.
reports.conclusion: Restrictive physiology with reduced diffusing capacity.

documents.title: Pulmonology Consultation
documents.author: pulmonology
documents.body:
Outside pulmonology consultation, date of service 08/11/2021.
Referred by primary care for progressive breathlessness.

History: About six months of steadily increasing shortness of breath with exertion and a dry, nonproductive cough. He has had no fevers, no chest pain and no recent travel. Long-standing COPD on 2 L continuous oxygen, tiotropium and salmeterol, albuterol by nebulizer as needed. Former smoker, around 45 pack-years, quit 2014. Former heavy alcohol use, abstinent since 2019, with compensated cirrhosis. Retired construction foreman; no known asbestos or silica exposure beyond the usual job-site dust. Father had COPD and lung cancer.
Medications: as listed by primary care, plus lisinopril, hydrochlorothiazide and metformin. Allergies: NKDA.

Exam: Digital clubbing. Fine inspiratory crackles at both lung bases. No wheeze. Heart regular, no edema.

Data: HRCT shows reticulation with honeycombing at the bases and in a subpleural distribution, with no embolism or acute process. Full PFTs show reduced lung volumes (TLC, FRC and RV all decreased) with preserved FEV1 and FVC and a raised FEV1/FVC ratio; DLCO is reduced.

Impression:
1. Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis. The CT pattern is typical, there is no clear exposure or connective tissue history, and the physiology is restrictive. In my view the fibrosis now dominates his lung mechanics, which is why the obstruction expected from his COPD is not evident on this study.
2. COPD with chronic hypoxemic respiratory failure, on oxygen.

Plan:
- Antifibrotic therapy (nintedanib or pirfenidone) discussed. Both carry hepatic risk and are not advised with his cirrhosis; we agreed not to start either for now.
- Continue oxygen 2 L and current inhalers.
- Repeat HRCT in about one year; follow-up here every 6 months.
- Vaccinations per primary care.

Pulmonology

documents.title: Primary Care Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Routine f/u, but the main thing today: since about July, food sticks - meat and bread mostly, liquids fine. Sometimes undigested food comes back up hours later, especially when he lies down at night. Feels a lump in his throat. Ingrid says his breath has been bad. No weight loss by our scale. No pain with swallowing.

Exam: neck supple, no mass felt. Oropharynx clear. Lungs - crackles at bases as before. Heart regular.

A/P
1. Dysphagia to solids with regurgitation of undigested food and halitosis - sounds oropharyngeal/upper esophageal, Zenker on the list. Referred to GI (he already knows the liver group's GI colleagues). Small bites, sit up after meals meanwhile.
2. COPD/IPF - stable, pulm in February.
3. HTN, DM - labs today.
Shingrix #2 today. RTC 3 mo.
